meta.move: Written by the lead after attempt 1 (not blind): owns the zero, shows each piece by saying so, answers each defence in a sentence, offers 4.4, sets a date
meta.expect: She reaches the deal after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
Who decided Owen's essay was worth a zero, and when?
Thanks for coming in. Before anything else: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. That was wrong, and Owen shouldn't have found out on his phone.
Okay. Now, on what basis?

I've turned my laptop to you. This is the document's version history: created Wednesday, October 28, at 11:31 PM with a title only. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in one edit. At 11:58 PM, another 794 words in one edit. No earlier drafts.
11:31, 11:52, 11:58. He could have written it somewhere else and pasted it in. That's a version history, not a finding, and your own procedure says you speak to the student first.
If he drafted it somewhere else, he can bring that draft with its date and I'll look at it. Until then, this record is what we have.
Fine, Hale. Whatever comes of this, it stays off his record and it stays quiet. What else do you have?
Here's the essay, page two, and here's the play open to Act 3, Scene 2. The essay quotes 'The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile.' Search the scene yourself; it isn't there.
Different editions, Hale. Is it anywhere in the play?
A misquote from memory is usually close to a real line. This one isn't close to anything in the play.
I'll search the whole text tonight. Assume it isn't there. So what do you want from Owen?
Here's his October 15 outline beside the essay. The outline argues Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay. That's called revising.

Here's what I can offer under procedure 4.4: a private supervised rewrite, after school, not in front of his class, before December 1. The new mark replaces the zero, and nothing goes on his record. I'll put that in writing tonight.
That's 4.4, in writing tonight, and nothing on his record. He'll do the rewrite to put this behind him, not because he did anything. Give me a date before December 1.
Thursday the twelfth after school works for me. Does that work for Owen?
Thursday the twelfth. I'll confirm with Owen tonight, and put the date in your email.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

In today's meeting you agreed under procedure 4.4 to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday, November 12, with its mark replacing the zero and nothing placed on Owen's record. I still require that agreement, including the date, confirmed to me in writing. I expect it tonight, as you said.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: She reached her last position and agreed to a private supervised rewrite after school on Thursday the twelfth with nothing on his record, and she still wants that confirmed in writing tonight; that is the fair outcome under procedure 4.4, and you reached it before her time ran out.
What moved her: Turning the screen to show the version history with its exact times, because she could check it herself and you answered her pasted-from-elsewhere defence by asking for a dated draft.
What cost ground: Nothing; your outline comparison was your weakest piece and she brushed it off as revision, but by then the first two pieces already stood.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history put the essay late on the night of October 28, the night before it was due, close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, but it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she said your own procedure requires speaking to the student first, answer whether you spoke to Owen before entering the zero, because she never got an answer to that and it is the question she will take to the principal.
